sections.html:
Compact Salem occupies roughly 14.5 square miles of the Roanoke Valley, around 1,175 feet above sea level, as an independent city. It sits beside the city of Roanoke, and Roanoke County wraps around it. The city grew up along the Great Road, which later became US 11 and then Interstate 81, so many blocks run along an old east and west line, with Main Street in the middle and Roanoke College one block north.

The layout means short drives. Most houses are within a few minutes of Main Street, the interstate and Roanoke.

sections.h2: An independent city that is also a county seat
sections.html:
No county includes Salem. Independence came on December 31, 1967, and since then city offices have done the work a county would do elsewhere. Confusingly, Salem remains the seat of Roanoke County, yet the governments are distinct. Salem keeps its own courthouse and sheriff's office, shares a jail with the county, and sees the county's administrative offices located in Cave Spring beyond the city line.

For city taxes, permits and utilities, you deal with Salem, even though a Roanoke County address may show up on some mail. When a bill, notice or lien arrives, check which government sent it before you pay.

The city took in South Salem in 1953 and an eastern tract in 1960, so houses were built in stages across the twentieth century. Repair needs vary by decade, from old wiring and plumbing in the earliest blocks to newer roofs that still need work.

Seniors made up 21.0% of the 2020 population, and close to a third of households were one person living alone. Houses regularly come up for sale after an owner dies, enters assisted living or moves in with relatives. The heirs frequently live out of state and have no interest in handling repairs, a vacant house and probate dates from far away.

In that spot, a direct cash sale can make the road shorter. The buyer accepts the house in its present condition and the two of you talk through the closing date.

sections.h2: Roads, the college and event traffic
sections.html:
The old Great Road corridor, now US 11, and Interstate 81 both cross the city. Roanoke College, in central Salem, was chartered in 1853 after the Virginia Institute moved from Staunton in 1847. Salem Football Stadium hosted the NCAA Division III championship game, the Stagg Bowl, from 1993 to 2016, and the Salem Civic Center and the James I. Moyer Sports Complex have hosted other NCAA events.

Blocks close to the college and the civic venues get extra traffic and event parking, and buyers will likely raise it.

Salem operates its own school system: four elementary schools (G. W. Carver, South Salem, East Salem and West Salem), Andrew Lewis Middle School and Salem High School. Government follows the council-manager model, in which a five-member council picks a mayor and vice mayor from within and a city manager oversees the day-to-day work.

Questions about permits, code complaints, utility accounts and tax bills go to Salem's own departments, not Roanoke County.

sections.h2: Taxes and fees when you sell
sections.html:
Two deed taxes apply to a Virginia sale. First comes the state recordation tax, 25 cents per $100 of the price or assessed value, whichever is higher, under section 58.1-801.

Second is the grantor's tax in section 58.1-802, at 50 cents per $500 of value above $100. Sellers usually owe it, but the two sides may agree the buyer takes some or all. Page one of the deed has to show the price before the clerk records it.

  • Have the title company prorate city taxes at the table.
  • Confirm current recording charges with the circuit court clerk who records Salem deeds.
  • Phone the City of Salem Treasurer or Commissioner of the Revenue for property tax due dates.

Estates get different treatment in one respect. The Residential Property Disclosure Act leaves out transfers made by a fiduciary running a decedent's estate, a guardianship, a conservatorship or a trust. The exclusions in section 55.1-702 also cover transfers between spouses or to lineal relatives, and transfers after a foreclosure sale.

Honesty with a buyer is still required. The usual seller disclosure form may just not fit an executor's sale, so have the estate's attorney say which rules cover your transfer before you sign.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Salem
sections.html:
Contract, title search, deed and recording all work the way they do for any Virginia sale. The one thing missing is the buyer's lender.

  • Send the address, a description of the house and your timing.
  • After our review, an offer reflects the house in its current state.
  • A title company looks for liens and drafts the deed.
  • You pick a closing day, sign and take your proceeds.

Take a photo ID, your deed if you hold a copy and mortgage details. Landlords add the lease. Turning down an offer costs nothing.

sections.h2: Paying off liens and back taxes at closing
sections.html: Owing a bill or carrying a lien will not block a sale. The title company discovers what is attached to the property, and each amount is settled out of your proceeds as shown on the settlement statement. Salem and Roanoke County are separate governments, so work out which one sent each notice, then ask that office for a payoff figure. With those numbers early, you can weigh an offer by what you would really receive, not by its headline.

sections.h2: Getting an older Salem house ready to show
sections.html: Even if you plan to sell as is, a few inexpensive steps help any buyer see the house clearly. Clear the walkways, open the blinds and make sure the utilities are on for the visit. Gather what you know about the roof, the heating and cooling system and the plumbing, since buyers in older neighborhoods ask about those first. If you would rather not do any of it, a cash buyer takes the house as it stands.

Listing in the traditional way means getting the house ready, hosting showings, haggling over repairs after the inspection and waiting for the buyer's lender. A cash sale avoids the lender and usually the haggling.

  • A listing fits a house in good shape when you are willing to wait for the best price.
  • Selling by owner saves the agent's commission, though marketing and paperwork fall to you.
  • A cash offer fits inherited, tenant-occupied, damaged or behind-on-payments houses, where speed and certainty outrank top dollar.

Whichever way you go, compare the amount that would reach you after taxes, repairs and carrying costs.

faqs.q: Is Salem, Virginia part of Roanoke County?
faqs.a: No. Salem is an independent city and a separate jurisdiction, though it is the county seat of Roanoke County. It has its own courthouse and sheriff's office, and the county's administrative offices are in Cave Spring.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed taxes when a house sells in Salem?
faqs.a: The seller normally pays the grantor's tax of 50 cents per $500, and the state recordation tax of 25 cents per $100 is charged on the deed. The buyer and seller can agree to shift the grantor's tax. Your closing statement shows the exact amounts.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house in Salem without a listing?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the person signing has legal authority to sell, such as an executor or a named heir after the estate is settled. Confirm with the estate's attorney before you accept any offer.

faqs.q: How fast can a cash sale close in Salem?
faqs.a: Timing depends on title work, liens, probate status and when you want to move. A cash buyer does not wait on a mortgage underwriter, so the title search often sets the date.

faqs.q: Where do I find Salem's current property tax due dates?
faqs.a: Ask the City of Salem Treasurer or Commissioner of the Revenue.
